current_bottleneck: Native joint38 generation is finite and mechanically one-model, but it attenuates cross-factor dependence and produces overly wide anchor-factor tail changes. The likely mechanism is data-coordinate mismatch: 609/625 learn state-level paths after empirical-score normalization, while risk scenarios are naturally laws over encoded daily changes integrated back to levels.
last_result_summary: 627a audited 610a, 612a, and 625a on the actual joint38 panel. 610a/612a pass anchor daily-change KS for 11/13 factors but have q99 change ratios above target and compressed dependence. 625a improves IV-factor correlation shape but worsens factor KS to 8/13 and still compresses absolute correlation magnitudes. No native joint candidate is yet risk-manager deployable as a calibrated joint law.
next_step_recommendation: Run 628a as a clean coordinate reset: train one native joint AR transition law on unified encoded daily changes for all 38 channels, then reconstruct levels by integrating changes and evaluate both IV full-suite behavior and joint-panel dependence. This tests the user's concern that anchor factors should be generated as changes without adding IV/factor-specific branches.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
